title: QBR - Lumina Commerce - Health & Roadmap Review
summary: Quarterly health check focusing on steady growth in inference volume, higher-than-expected token costs in month-to-month spikes, a recent infra incident tied to an autoscaler bug, and interest in piloting Private (VPC) due to data residency and SSO requirements. SE agreed to run a cost/latency benchmarking spreadsheet and CSM to propose a roadmap cadence. Action items captured at end.
next_steps: Redwood to share cost optimization spreadsheet and recommended batching/quantization settings by 2026-03-18
Schedule private deployment pilot scoping session w/ Lumina infra team (proposed week of 2026-03-22)
Redwood SE to run end-to-end latency benchmark across EU region and share results
action_items: Maya Chen - Send pricing + cost optimization spreadsheet - due 2026-03-18
Liam Ortiz - Run EU latency + throughput benchmark and attach raw logs - due 2026-03-19
Priya Nair - Draft QBR follow-up deck and tentative pilot plan - due 2026-03-17
Daniel Park - Share compliance contact and preferred KMS vendor info - due 2026-03-16
transcript: Meeting header: 2026-03-11 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Recording: yes
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Daniel Park: Daniel here, hi Maya.
[00:07] Sarah Lee: Sarah, hi all.
[00:09] Aisha Khan: Aisha here.
[00:11] Liam Ortiz: Liam from Redwood, SE.
[00:13] Priya Nair: Priya, CSM at Redwood.

[00:18] Maya Chen: Cool. Agenda — usage and costs, reliability incidents, roadmap, and pilot discussion for private deployment. We'll spend ~15 on usage/costs, 15 on reliability, then roadmap and next steps.
[01:02] Sarah Lee: Quick note, we saw a 30% bump in token volume during the promo last month. Most came from chat recommendations which are high context length so tokens spiked.
[01:20] Maya Chen: Got it. Do you have the breakdown by model/route?
[01:25] Sarah Lee: Yeah, attached in the share, but rough split is 70% on redwood-hosted gpt-4 style open model and 30% on smaller embedding calls. The embed calls are cheaper but frequent.
[01:42] Aisha Khan: Also, we noticed a couple of 5xx spikes on 2/27 that correlated with an autoscaler restart.

[01:50] Liam Ortiz: I pulled traces; the autoscaler hit a transient quota sync issue which triggered a restart loop for some Dedicated nodes. We pushed a hotfix, but there was a ~18 minute window with degraded throughput.
[02:05] Daniel Park: That outage impacted checkout recommendations; we hit our retry budget and saw increased latency. Our SREs would like more granular alerting on queue depth.
[02:20] Priya Nair: Noted — we can add queue-depth alerts and expose the per-route token backlog in the console. We'll propose thresholds in the follow-up.

[03:10] Sarah Lee: On costs, the unexpected thing was the token mix; promt engineering reduced average token per call for chat, but the new persona flow increased output length. Is there an easy lever?

[03:25] Liam Ortiz: Yes — batching and prefix caching would help. Right now you're not using prefix KV cache aggressively; some of the chat history is re-sent every request. We can recommend a caching profile — e g, 90% hit expected on session re-use.
[03:40] Sarah Lee: How much would quantization impact quality? We tried int8 previously and saw slight latency improvements but some hallucination increase.

[03:50] Liam Ortiz: Tradeoff is model dependent. For your workloads we recommend dynamic quantization with 4-bit eval in non-critical routes. We'll share model-specific QoE numbers in the spreadsheet.
[04:12] Maya Chen: Priya will send the cost workbook with recommended batching/windowing/quantization by next Thursday.
[05:00] Aisha Khan: On compliance — we need SOC two artifacts, audit logs, and KMS integration details. Also looking at V P C peering for data residency in EU.
[05:15] Maya Chen: Understood. We have the SOC 2 pack and KMS integration docs — I'll drop the links. For V P C private pilot, SE will scope network requirements next week.
[06:30] Daniel Park: Our legal team also wants retention settings — can we pin logs to 90 days and configurable export?

[06:45] Priya Nair: Yes, retention is configurable on Private and Dedicated; for hosted we have standard retention but enterprise add-on supports longer retention and export. I'll include that in the deck.
[07:20] Sarah Lee: Roadmap — any upcoming features that help cost or reliability?

[07:28] Liam Ortiz: We're rolling out smarter routing policies next quarter that can route by latency SLO or cost tier; also an automatic fallback to a quantized variant if Dedicated capacity is constrained. There was a mention of kernel-level optimizations for long sequence lengths too.
[07:50] Sarah Lee: Nice. That routing policy could let us keep high quality for checkout paths and cheaper variants for exploratory queries.
[08:10] Daniel Park: For the pilot, our requirements: EU data residency, SSO (SAML), KMS integration with Azure Key Vault, and control over retention. Lead time and cost estimate?

[08:28] Maya Chen: Typical pilot baseline is 6 weeks for V P C setup + validation. We'll provide a draft SOW; cost varies by node count, but we'll propose a minimal Reserved capacity for the pilot to make numbers predictable.
[09:05] Aisha Khan: Can Redwood support canary rollouts and A/B testing during the pilot?

[09:12] Liam Ortiz: Yes — rollouts and traffic shifting are supported in the console; we can set automatic fallback to hosted if backend capacity dips. We did want to validate latency under EU region loads, which we'll run as part of the benchmark.
[10:00] Sarah Lee: About the incident — do you have the postmortem?

[10:07] Priya Nair: Short postmortem sent 48 hours after incident; it lists root cause as quota-sync race in the autoscaler. Long term fix is in staging and we scheduled an incremental deploy. I'll re-share the PM and include the timeline.
[11:15] Daniel Park: Good. For monitoring, can we get token-level breakdowns by route and model?
[11:25] Liam Ortiz: Yes. The Console exposes per-route token cost and latency percentiles. We'll also export a CSV of the last 90 days if you want to plug into BI.
[12:05] Sarah Lee: A quick clarification — you said prefix caching might cause token double-counting?

[12:12] Liam Ortiz: No; it reduces tokens sent. What sometimes happens is double-counting in analytics when sessions are duplicated in instrumentation; we'll look at your instrumentation to ensure events map 1:1.

[13:00] Maya Chen: Quick recap — action items and timeline. Priya will draft the follow-up deck, Maya will send SOC2/KMS links, Liam will run benchmarks, and Maya will propose pilot SOW. Any objections?
[13:18] Daniel Park: None from us. One ask — can you include a cost estimate for Reserved vs on-demand for Dedicated for our average 24/7 load?
[13:28] Liam Ortiz: Yes, that'll be in the cost workbook with an amortized per-token number and breakeven horizon.
[14:05] Sarah Lee: Also please include recommended quantization profiles per model and expected QoE drop numbers.
[14:12] Liam Ortiz: Will do. We'll include examples: int8 for non-critical, 4-bit for background routes, and the measured latency/accuracy deltas.
[15:00] Aisha Khan: For the pilot network, we will need a list of CIDR ranges and supported peering options; please include that in the SOW.
[15:12] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll include CIDRs, peering steps, and a checklist for firewall rules.
[15:50] Daniel Park: Timeline constraints — we need pilot in place before the European marketing push in early May. That gives ~8 weeks. Is that realistic?
[15:58] Liam Ortiz: Yes, 6–8 weeks is typical; we'll aim for the shorter side but will list pre-reqs that could add time.
[16:40] Maya Chen: Anything else on reliability or SLA?
[16:45] Sarah Lee: Could we get a tailored SLA for checkout path?
[16:50] Maya Chen: Enterprise add-on can include route-specific SLOs and incident response SLA; we'll surface options in the SOW.
[18:00] Priya Nair: I'll schedule the pilot scoping session and include Lumina infra and legal. Proposed week of 2026-03-22 — does that work?
[18:10] Daniel Park: Works for us.

[18:30] Maya Chen: Okay, final recap: deliverables and owners — Priya: deck + pilot schedule; Maya: SOC2/KMS links + pricing; Liam: benchmarks + cost workbook + quantization recommendations; Daniel: compliance contact and KMS vendor. We'll sync next on 2026-03-18 for a short check-in. Thanks all.
[19:00] Meeting ends.
